Standardize SUS data column names and values

Source: R/sus_data_standardize.R
sus_data_standardize.Rd

This function standardizes column names and categorical values in SUS datasets, ensuring consistency across different years and versions. It supports three languages: English (en), Portuguese (pt), and Spanish (es).

Usage

sus_data_standardize(
  df,
  lang = "pt",
  translate_columns = TRUE,
  standardize_values = TRUE,
  keep_original = FALSE,
  backend = "arrow",
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

df

A climasus_df, tibble or data frame (typically from sus_data_import() / sus_data_clean_encoding()), or a lazy Arrow dataset. The health system (SIM, SINAN, SIH, SIA, CNES, SINASC) is detected from the column names, or taken from sus_meta.

lang

Character scalar, "pt" (default), "en" or "es". Language of the translated column names, standardized categorical values and messages; other values abort.

translate_columns

Logical scalar, default TRUE. Rename the original DATASUS columns to descriptive names in lang.

standardize_values

Logical scalar, default TRUE. Recode categorical values (e.g. sex, race, education) to labels in lang.

keep_original

Logical scalar, default FALSE. If TRUE, keep the original columns alongside the standardized ones.

backend

Character scalar, "arrow" (default) or "tibble". "arrow" processes lazily and falls back to "tibble" (in memory) with a warning if it fails; "tibble" processes in memory.

verbose

Logical scalar, default TRUE. Print a report of the standardization actions.

Value

A climasus_df with standardized column names and values in lang (a lazy Arrow table if the input was lazy and the arrow backend succeeded). sus_meta: stage = "stand", system preserved/detected.

Details

The function builds upon the preprocessing done by microdatasus, adding an additional layer of standardization specifically designed for climate-health research workflows.

Pipeline position: after sus_data_clean_encoding(), before the filtering (sus_data_filter_cid(), sus_data_filter_demographics()) and sus_data_create_variables() steps. Column names change with lang, so use the same lang in the following steps.

References

Brazilian Ministry of Health. DATASUS. http://datasus.saude.gov.br

SALDANHA, Raphael de Freitas; BASTOS, Ronaldo Rocha; BARCELLOS, Christovam. Microdatasus: pacote para download e pre-processamento de microdados do Departamento de Informatica do SUS (DATASUS). Cad. Saude Publica, Rio de Janeiro , v. 35, n. 9, e00032419, 2019. Available from https://doi.org/10.1590/0102-311x00032419.

See also

sus_data_clean_encoding(), sus_data_filter_cid(), sus_data_create_variables()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Standardize to English
df_en <- sus_data_standardize(df_raw, lang = "en")

# Standardize to Portuguese
df_pt <- sus_data_standardize(df_raw, lang = "pt")

# Standardize to Spanish
df_es <- sus_data_standardize(df_raw, lang = "es")

# Keep original columns for comparison
df_both <- sus_data_standardize(
  df_raw,
  lang = "pt",
  keep_original = TRUE
)

# Only translate column names (not values)
df_cols_only <- sus_data_standardize(
  df_raw,
  lang = "en",
  translate_columns = TRUE,
  standardize_values = FALSE
)

# Complete pipeline
df_analysis_ready <- sus_data_import(uf = "SP", year = 2023, system = "SIM-DO") |>
  sus_data_clean_encoding() |>
  sus_data_standardize(lang = "pt")
} # }
